notes: Hand-authored mapping from the vendored packs (sources.json / pack.json) onto the assembler-v2 basis registry: which style lane a model belongs to, which head family / body archetype it stands in for, how it mounts onto the rig, and how each of its glTF material slots maps onto the 11 palette regions. build-lanes.mjs validates every reference against the committed pack.json manifests and emits assets/packs/lanes.json (read by scripts/pack_library.gd) plus the frontend's generated catalog, so the engine, the UI and this file can never drift.

kaykit-adventurers-v1.reason: SINGLE 1024-class baked atlas per character and NO named material slots, so swap_materials() cannot reach it: binding that one material to a flat house colour paints the whole character one colour. That is why this pack shipped with recolour switched off, recorded as a capability gap whose fix 'needs the atlas cell layout, an art task'. It is not an art task. The atlas is PALETTE-INDEXED (measured: PNG colortype 3, 198-256 entries) and the vendor splits every character into SEMANTIC MESH NODES, so each node's texels are a luminance ramp of one hue - the Knight's head is a 16-entry flesh ramp, its cape a 13-entry red one. The region colour therefore replaces the HUE per node while the atlas keeps supplying the SHADING, with no new texture and no re-UVing. The engine measures each node's dominant hue and how much of the node it covers, and recolours only texels near that hue - a node that mixes two materials (the Mage's 'Head' node is 36% single-hue because it carries the hood AND the face) keeps its vendor colours rather than being painted one wrong colour. mount_report().atlasRegions says exactly what recoloured.

kaykit-skeletons-v1.reason: Same single-atlas texturing and the same semantic mesh-node split as the Adventurers pack, so the same per-node recolour applies. The skeletons additionally separate Skull/Jaw/Eyes as their own nodes, which is why the bone tone and the socket glow recolour independently.

polygonalmind-100avatars-v1.reason: Each avatar bakes to one atlas material (mat_NNN); the same atlas problem as KayKit. Scoped to the VRM importer corpus anyway, not to player avatars.

khronos-fox-v1.reason: One textured material on a 576-tri quadruped; it is the runtime-loader reference asset, not a player avatar.

blocked.verdict: NOT SHIPPED - no boundary in these files corresponds to a MATERIAL region.
blocked.evidence: The KayKit half of this gap is CLOSED (materialPolicy 'atlas'). The 100Avatars line is a different case, and every candidate boundary was measured across all 8 shipped avatars. (1) STRUCTURE: 1 mesh node, 1 mesh, 1 PRIMITIVE and 1 material per file - the primitive count is the check an earlier audit skipped, and it confirms the block rather than lifting it; no COLOR_0 vertex attribute exists on any file, so there is no per-vertex region signal either. (2) VRM METADATA carries nothing the glTF does not: firstPerson.meshAnnotations is empty on all 8 (so not even the head is annotated), secondaryAnimation boneGroups and colliderGroups are empty, every blendShape group has zero materialValues, and the single VRM materialProperties entry points _MainTex and _ShadeTexture at the SAME image - MToon's base/shade split separates by light direction, not by body part. (3) BONE WEIGHT, the one route that would have worked: the mesh DOES split geometrically by humanoid bone group (jimmy: head 1411 / torso 123 / arm 864 / leg 142 vertices), so CharForgeMeshSurgery could cut it up - but those groups are ANATOMICAL, not material. One head group carries face, hair, hat and eyes together, so recolouring by it paints a face the colour of its hair. Nor can hue separate them inside a group: the groups SHARE atlas texels heavily, with as little as 2% of a group's texels exclusive to it (skelly head 2%, cactusboy head 2%, jimmy torso 7%). (4) Two of the eight (100avatars_010_froggy, 100avatars_051_polybot) are JPEG, not palette-indexed PNG, so they are not index-separable at all.
blocked.blocker: There is no semantic source to derive a region assignment from. Every boundary these files expose - node, primitive, material, VRM annotation, bone group - is either absent or anatomical rather than material. Recolouring them would need a per-texel region map authored by hand (an index->region LUT plus a shipped index texture), i.e. real art work per avatar, and it would still not cover the two JPEG-textured ones.
blocked.shippedInstead: The vendor material is preserved and the UI marks these entries 'fixed colours'. They are the BYO-VRM importer's reference corpus rather than player avatars, so this costs the character editor nothing.
